prompt: How do I use the slide master in PowerPoint?
completion:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** for using the Slide Master in PowerPoint.  
It covers the most common tasks—adding a logo, changing fonts, setting a background, and applying a layout to existing slides—so you can keep your presentation consistent and make large‑scale edits in seconds.

---

## 1.  What Is a Slide Master?

| **Slide Master** | **Layout Slide** | **Content Slide** |
|------------------|------------------|-------------------|
| The *highest‑level* master that defines the overall look (background, fonts, colors, placeholders). | Child layouts that inherit the master but can tweak elements (e.g., hide a placeholder, change placeholder type). | The individual slides you see in the normal view. They use a layout, which in turn uses the master. |

*Why use it?*  
- Edit once → changes propagate everywhere.  
- Keep brand consistency (logo, footer).  
- Create reusable templates.

---

## 2.  Open Slide Master View

| **PowerPoint 2013‑2021 / Office 365** | **PowerPoint Online** |
|---------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| 1. `View` tab → `Slide Master` | 1. `View` → `Slide Master` |
| 2. PowerPoint 2010 | 2. PowerPoint 2007 (`View` → `Slide Master`) |

> **Tip:** When you’re done, click **Close Master View** (or `Slide Master` → `Close Master View`) to return to the normal slide editor.

---

## 3.  Basic Master‑Slide Tasks

### 3.1  Add a Global Logo or Footer

1. In Slide Master view, click the **topmost** master slide (the one with the largest thumbnail).
2. `Insert` → `Picture` → choose your logo file.  
   *Drag it to the desired corner.*
3. **Resize** it and use the “Size & Position” dialog (`Format` → `Size & Position`) to lock its placement.
4. To make it appear on every slide, make sure the logo **doesn’t** belong to any *layout* placeholders.  
   *(If you accidentally inserted it on a layout, it will appear only on that layout.)*

### 3.2  Set a Unified Background

- `Design` → `Format Background`.  
  *Or* right‑click on the master slide → `Format Background`.  
- Choose a solid fill, gradient, picture, or texture.  
- Click **Apply to All** (or **Apply** if you’re already in master view) so that every layout inherits the background.

### 3.3  Change Theme Fonts & Colors

- `Slide Master` tab → **Edit Theme** group.  
  - **Fonts** → pick a built‑in set or `Customize Fonts…` for your own.
  - **Colors** → choose a built‑in color scheme or `Customize Colors…`.

> *All text placeholders automatically use the selected theme fonts.*

### 3.4  Add Placeholders

1. In a layout (or the master) that you want to modify, click **Insert Placeholder** → choose `Text`, `Picture`, `Chart`, etc.  
2. Drag the placeholder to the desired spot.  
3. In the **Layout** tab, you can set its alignment, lock it, or set default text (right‑click → `Placeholder Settings`).

### 3.5  Hide Elements on Specific Layouts

- Select the element (e.g., a placeholder or a shape) on a layout you want to hide it from.  
- Right‑click → **Hide Placeholder** (for placeholders) or **Hide** (for shapes).  
- It remains in the master but disappears from that layout.

---

## 4.  Applying a Master Layout to Existing Slides

1. Return to normal view (`Close Master View`).  
2. Right‑click a slide you want to re‑style → `Layout`.  
3. Pick the layout from the list.  
   - All slides that already use that layout will update automatically.  
   - If you want *every* slide to adopt the same layout, **select all slides** (`Ctrl+A`) and then pick the layout.

> **Quick Reapply**  
> The master view has a `Reapply` button. If you’ve changed a layout in master view and need to update an individual slide, right‑click the slide → `Reapply Layout`.

---

## 5.  Advanced Tips

| Task | How to Do It | Why It Helps |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| **Create a Custom Theme** | `Slide Master` → `Themes` → `Save Current Theme…` | Reuse branding across multiple presentations. |
| **Multiple Masters** | `Slide Master` → `Insert Slide Master` | One master for title slides, another for body slides (useful for large decks). |
| **Add Slide Numbers** | `Insert` → `Slide Number` → choose `Slide Number` and/or `Date & Time`. | Adds page numbers automatically. |
| **Link to Master Slides** | `Slide Master` → `Insert Slide Master` → drag elements between masters | Keep layout logic clean and modular. |
| **Export Master as a Template** | `File` → `Save As` → choose `PowerPoint Template (*.potx)` | Share a ready‑to‑use brand template with others. |
| **Reset Slide** | Right‑click a slide → `Reset Slide` | Reverts all custom formatting back to master defaults. |
| **Use Master for Slide Background Video** | `Insert` → `Video` → `Video on My PC` → then `Format` → `Send to Back` → `Underlay Video` | Background videos stay consistent. |

---

## 6.  Common Gotchas & Fixes

| Issue | Likely Cause | Fix |
|-------|--------------|-----|
| Logo disappears on some slides | It’s on a layout you didn’t apply | Move logo to master slide (topmost) or apply the layout to those slides |
| Font changes only on new slides | Slide uses a custom style (e.g., “Title 2” that was edited directly) | Right‑click the text box → `Reset` to inherit master font |
| Background shows on new slides but not old ones | Old slides were saved before you applied the background | Apply layout again or `Reset Slide` |
| Placeholders show “Click to add text” even after editing | You edited the placeholder directly (not the master) | Edit in Slide Master, not the content slide |

---

## 7.  Quick Checklist

- [ ] Open **Slide Master** view.  
- [ ] Edit the **topmost master** for brand elements (logo, background, colors, fonts).  
- [ ] Customize individual **layouts** as needed (placeholders, visibility).  
- [ ] Apply layouts to existing slides (`Ctrl+A` → choose layout).  
- [ ] Close Master View and verify changes propagate.  
- [ ] Save the file (or as a template).

---

### Final Thought

Think of the Slide Master as the *global stylesheet* of a website. One small tweak, and everything changes instantly. Once you’re comfortable with the master view, most design work becomes a matter of “Set once, apply everywhere.” Happy presenting!
